i18n:
3.1 Overview of the Language System

The ABpE Portal supports multilingual interfaces (Internationalization / i18n). All texts in the user interface are loaded from JSON files organized by language. The system is designed so that new languages can be added simply by creating a new directory – without code changes.

3.2 Directory Structure of Language Files

static/abpe_ui/i18n/
├── de/                          # German
│   ├── meta.json                # Language metadata
│   ├── core-common.json         # Global labels (Buttons, Navigation)
│   ├── ui-components.json       # UI component texts
│   ├── api-messages.json        # API error messages
│   └── modules/                 # Module-specific translations
│       └── documentation.json
├── en/                          # English (same structure)
└── fr/                          # French (same structure)

3.3 The meta.json – Language Metadata

Each language directory contains a meta.json with metadata about the language:

{
    "code": "de",
    "name": "German",
    "native": "Deutsch",
    "flag": "🇩🇪",
    "direction": "ltr",
    "version": "1.0",
    "author": "ABpE Team",
    "last_updated": "2026-05-15",
    "enabled": true,
    "fallback": "de",
    "completeness": 100
}

This metadata is read by the API /api/available-languages/ and used in the language dropdown.

3.4 Structure of Translation Files

The translation files are simple JSON files with key-value pairs:

{
    "dashboard": "Dashboard",
    "help": "Help",
    "save": "Save"
}

Nested structures are also possible:

{
    "dashboard": {
        "title": "Dashboard",
        "welcome": "Welcome back"
    }
}

3.5 The Fallback Cascade

The language selection follows a defined priority (fallback cascade):

  1. User Profile (if logged in) – preference stored in the database
  2. Session – temporary language choice during the session
  3. Browser (Accept-Language Header) – browser language
  4. System Default – from settings.py (DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = 'de')
  5. Hard Fallback – 'de' (always present)

3.6 Loading Translations (JavaScript)

The JavaScript module core-language.js is responsible for loading and applying translations:

async function loadLanguage(lang, moduleId = null) {
    // 1. Load global translations
    await loadFile(lang, 'core-common.json');
    await loadFile(lang, 'ui-components.json');
    await loadFile(lang, 'api-messages.json');
    
    // 2. Load module-specific translations (if available)
    if (moduleId) {
        await loadFile(lang, `modules/${moduleId}.json`);
    }
    
    // 3. Apply translations in the DOM
    applyTranslations();
}

3.7 Usage in HTML (data-i18n)

In HTML, texts are marked with the data-i18n attribute:

<h1 data-i18n="dashboard.title">Dashboard</h1>
<button data-i18n="save">Save</button>

JavaScript then replaces the content of the elements with the translation from the loaded JSON file.

3.8 Language Switching in the Frontend

Language switching is done via the language dropdown in the header. When a language is clicked, an AJAX request is sent to /api/set-language/, which stores the language in the session. Subsequently, the new translations are loaded and the DOM is updated – without a page reload.

3.9 Adding a New Language

To add a new language (e.g., Spanish), the following steps are necessary:

  1. Create directory: i18n/es/
  2. Copy meta.json from de/ and adapt it
  3. Translate core-common.json
  4. Translate ui-components.json
  5. For each module: translate modules/{module}.json
  6. Run collectstatic
  7. The new language will appear automatically in the dropdown

3.10 Handling Missing Translations

If a translation for a key is not found in the current language, the system falls back as follows:

  • First, it searches in common.json of the current language
  • Then in the fallback language (defined in meta.json)
  • Finally, the key itself is displayed as text (e.g., [missing: dashboard.title])
